content: The test image shows dry, bleached white soybean stems with numerous small black structures (pycnidia) visible on the stem surface, and some dark areas. This strongly suggests a late-season stem disease. Top candidates: **Diaporthe** (parallel rows of black pycnidia on mature stems) or **Anthracnose** (dark acervuli on stems).

The Diaporthe reference (bottom-right panel) shows bleached white stems with black pycnidia in oval/ring patterns — nearly identical to the test image. The test image matches Diaporthe very closely: dry bleached stem, characteristic black flask-shaped pycnidia visible on stem surface.

The Anthracnose reference shows more brown/golden pods and stems with darker acervuli — does not match the bleached white stem with ring-patterned pycnidia in the test image.

Brown Stem Rot shows internal brown pith discoloration and leaf chlorosis — clearly not matching. 

The test image is definitively **Diaporthe**: bleached white mature stems with characteristic black oval/ring-patterned pycnidia visible on the stem surface — an exact match to the Diaporthe reference bottom-right panel and its description of "parallel rows of black, flask-shaped pycnidia on mature soybean stems at R6-R8 growth stages."
